title: The Investigating Tactile Experiences and Textures with Sustainable Materials in Art and Design Education
research_question: This study aims: (1) to explore tactile experiences with various sustainable materials; (2) to examine these materials through experiential learning practices to discover their potential in enhancing the creative process; and (3) to measure students' agreement using a questionnaire on tactile experiences with sustainable materials in educational settings, thereby promoting a participatory and tactile-focused learning approach.

participants.description: 48 student participants (42% male, 58% female). Majority below 20 years old (54%), followed by 20-25 years (40%), and 25 and above (6%). 94% had college education, 6% possessed education beyond college. Academic disciplines were primarily Art (54.17%) and Design (35.42%), with a smaller proportion in other fields (10.42%).
participants.recruitment: 45 students from Dhurakij Pundit University in Bangkok, Thailand (first-year and senior students) and 3 graduate students from other universities attending Bangkok Design Week.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Sustainable materials including Jesmonite, seashell waste, eggshell waste, coffee bean grounds, stucco, rice husk, bamboo fiber, and small natural pebbles. These were used in participatory workshops for students to experiment with and create diverse tactile textures.
Participatory workshops conducted in an environment conducive to experiential learning, tactile experience engagement, and detailed discussions.

measures.construct: Student perceptions and agreement levels regarding tactile experiences, sustainable materials, and art and design education.
measures.instrument: Online questionnaire using a 5-point Likert scale (1=extremely strong disagreement, 5=extremely strong agreement).

measures.construct: Expert insights on tactile experiences, sustainable materials, and their role in art and design education.
measures.instrument: In-depth interviews with three art and design experts (university professor, high school visual arts teacher, professional art director), consisting of five questions each.

measures.construct: Student engagement, creativity, understanding of sustainable materials, and tactile interactions.
measures.instrument: Observations and discussions during three participatory workshops where students collaborated on experimental solutions and presented their creations.

mechanisms: Tactile experiences are inherently complex and multifaceted, involving both physical interaction with materials and tactile connections, where the actions of touching and being touched are equally significant.
Sustainable materials provide unique sensory experiences that challenge conventional perceptions and encourage innovative thinking, thereby fostering creativity.
Experiential learning, particularly through participatory workshops, is a transformative process where knowledge is derived from active and emotional engagement with the material.

Students recognize the critical importance of tactile elements, such as textures, and the value of sustainable materials for environmental and community well-being, which enhances their understanding and appreciation of sustainability.
implementation_implications: Educational institutions, especially those focused on art and design, should incorporate tactile experiences with sustainable materials into their curriculum through participatory workshops, hands-on sessions, and project-based learning.
Further investigation into the psychological and emotional effects of tactile interaction with sustainable materials is recommended to offer valuable insights for enhancing educational strategies.

Exploring digital and virtual reality technologies to simulate tactile experiences with sustainable materials could extend the reach of experiential learning to long-distance learners and provide scalable solutions for institutions facing resource limitations.
Promote a deeper understanding of sustainability in art and design education and enhance the related literature.
Educate both students and instructors about the benefits and practical applications of sustainable materials.
Address challenges related to the availability and cost of sustainable materials to facilitate their broader use in educational settings.

limitations: Limited access to a wide variety of sustainable materials.
Issues like cost and availability of sustainable materials could limit students' use in schools.
Students' application of sustainable materials to art projects was limited despite their appreciation.
Existing literature has not sufficiently explored the role of tactile experiences with sustainable materials in art and design education.
Traditional discussions have focused on the environmental benefits of sustainable materials, often neglecting their educational and experiential value.
